originalSource.title: Orbit Studio Satellite Source of Truth v1.0.0 from GCAT satcat
originalSource.version: Package 1.0.0; GCAT satcat source header updated 2026-06-27 22:13:02 UTC

processing: The verified v1.0.0 package preserves the immutable 2026-06-27 GCAT satcat snapshot, its exact original checksum, normalized 69,703-record products, SQLite query database, 1957-2026 annual presence, reconstruction candidates, quality ledger, schemas, build scripts, and package checksums.

python3 data/satellite-source-of-truth/scripts/verify.py validates every package artifact checksum, database schema, record and class counts, annual summaries, snapshot membership, and the package-provided deterministic reconstruction angles.

scripts/build-satellite-web-catalog.py verifies the package first, queries only the canonical SQLite database, and deterministically exports all 69,620 Earth-associated payload, rocket-body, component, and debris rows into src/data/generated/satelliteCatalog.web.json.

Completed years use GCAT-derived present_at_period_end membership. The partial 2026 view uses the package-required snapshot_present_earth_objects membership and records the two-row reconciliation difference from the generic partial-year period-end flag.

The web export preserves GCAT JCAT and available SATCAT identities, classification, owner/status, lifecycle bounds, source perigee, source apogee, source inclination, source orbit epoch, and package reconstruction angles.

For historical rows without package-precomputed angles, the export applies the package-prescribed SHA-256 algorithm keyed by the stable JCAT identifier. Runtime code never creates a second hash or random reconstruction authority.

Twenty-one latest members and 244 all-history rows with insufficient or physically invalid orbital envelopes remain catalog-only. Displayed reconstructed states are not observed, live, current, or exact positions.

rights.licenseOrBasis: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0); GCAT expressly permits reproduction with citation.

release.restrictions: This is the complete packaged GCAT Earth-object membership for the supported four classes at the dated snapshot, not proof of operational status or observational completeness. Preserve attribution, source/reconstruction separation, partial-2026 semantics, catalog-only rows, package checksums, and the prohibition on live/exact wording.

originalSource.title: History of On-orbit Satellite Fragmentations, 16th Edition (NASA/TP-20220019160)
originalSource.publisher: NASA Orbital Debris Program Office, Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center

processing: Only the assessed-cause field is extracted: international designator, NORAD catalogue number, break-up date, and assessed cause. No document text, figure, or table layout is reproduced.

The reference's own DEBRIS CATALOGED and DEBRIS LEFT counts are deliberately not imported. They are correct for December 2022 and would contradict the 2026-06-27 GCAT snapshot; all fragment counts come from GCAT and only cause comes from this reference.

scripts/build-fragmentation-causes.py joins the extracted table to the web catalog on NORAD catalogue number and exact break-up date, so a parent that fragmented more than once cannot inherit another event's cause.

Join result: 198 of 1,034 GCAT fragmentation events (19.1%), covering 22,078 of 27,681 debris objects (79.8%). Events outside the reference are rendered as unassessed, which the interface keeps distinct from the reference's own UNKNOWN finding.
Extraction recovers 248 break-up events and is not claimed to be exhaustive; events it misses are absent rather than misattributed. See data/fragmentation-causes/PROVENANCE.md.

rights.licenseOrBasis: Work of the U.S. Government prepared by NASA; not subject to copyright protection in the United States (17 U.S.C. 105). Factual cause assessments only.
rights.attribution: Fragmentation cause assessments from NASA Orbital Debris Program Office, History of On-orbit Satellite Fragmentations, 16th Edition (NASA/TP-20220019160).
